simple.meaning: רִצְפָּה (ritspâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a hot stone ; also a tessellated pavement.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Chronicles 7:3. The surrounding context includes altar, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רִצְפָּה (H7531) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: רִצְפָּה (ritspâh) / H7531 is traced through 2 Chronicles 7:3, Esther 1:6, Isaiah 6:6, Ezekiel 40:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: All the children of Israel looked on, when the fire came down, and Yahweh’s glory was on the house. They bowed themselves with their faces to the ground on the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to Yahweh, saying,

There were hangings of white and blue material, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver, on a pavement of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.
Then he brought me into the outer court. Behold, there were rooms and a pavement made for the court all around. Thirty rooms were on the pavement.
Then he brought me into the outer court. Behold, there were rooms and a pavement made for the court all around. Thirty rooms were on the pavement.
The pavement was by the side of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates, even the lower pavement.
The pavement was by the side of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates, even the lower pavement.
Opposite the twenty cubits which belonged to the inner court, and opposite the pavement which belonged to the outer court, was gallery against gallery in the third floor.

definitions.short: a hot stone ; also a tessellated pavement
definitions.full: H7531. ritspah ִרצְפָה noun feminine pavement ; — absolute ׳ר Ezek 40:17 (twice in verse) +, construct ִרצְפַת Est 1:6 (van d. H. מַּת רִעצמָּה, -); — pavement , in Ezekiel's temple, Ezek 40:17 (twice in verse); 40:18 (twice in verse); 42:3 ; Solomon's temple 2Chr 7:3 ; in a palace Est 1:6 . I. רִצְמָּה noun feminine glowing stone (or coal) (We Israel u. Jüd. Geschichte. (3) 83); — ׳ר absolute Isa 6:6 ; plural רְצָפִים עֻגַת 1Kin 19:6 (compare Syriac above).
